expectedText:
PAID FAMILY LEAVE (PFL) — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's Paid Family Leave (PFL) program, a wage-replacement insurance benefit funded through State Disability Insurance (SDI) payroll deductions and administered by the Employment Development Department (EDD). PFL is a benefit program under the Unemployment Insurance Code, not a leave-granting law, and it operates separately from job-protected leave statutes such as the California Family Rights Act (CFRA) and the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA). Jordan Lee may be eligible to draw on PFL benefits during time away from work at Acme, Inc. for a qualifying reason, whether or not that time away is separately protected under CFRA, FMLA, or another leave law.

WHAT PAID FAMILY LEAVE IS
California's Paid Family Leave program — formally called Family Temporary Disability Insurance — is a wage-replacement benefit that is a component of the state's unemployment compensation disability insurance program. It is funded through employee contributions (State Disability Insurance, or SDI, payroll deductions) and is administered in accordance with the policies of that disability insurance program. The Unemployment Insurance Code separately establishes the Employment Development Department (EDD), within the Labor and Workforce Development Agency, as the state agency administering the state's unemployment and disability compensation programs, of which Paid Family Leave is a part.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Family Temporary Disability Insurance shall be known as Paid Family Leave."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3300(b) (leginfo text), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, legislative findings (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3300.)
  "The family temporary disability insurance program shall be a component of the state’s unemployment compensation disability insurance program, shall be funded through employee contributions, and shall be administered in accordance with the policies of the state disability insurance program created pursuant to this part."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3300(g) (leginfo text), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, legislative findings (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3300.)
  "There is in the Labor and Workforce Development Agency the Employment Development Department, which is vested with the duties, purposes, responsibilities, and jurisdiction heretofore exercised by the State Department of Benefit Payments or the California Health and Human Services Agency with respect to job creation activities."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 301 (leginfo text), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Employment Development Department, agency creation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=301.)
  Known gap: The citations to Section 3300(b) and 3300(g) are subsections of the same statutory section and are not independent of one another. Section 301 is a separate, independently numbered section, but it establishes the Employment Development Department generally for the whole Unemployment Insurance Code and doesn't itself mention Paid Family Leave by name — this document infers that 'the department' referenced throughout the Paid Family Leave chapter (for example, in its claim-filing deadline provisions) refers to the EDD established by Section 301, since Paid Family Leave sits within the same code division EDD administers. This document doesn't cover the specific procedure or website for filing a PFL claim with EDD.

WHAT PAID FAMILY LEAVE BENEFITS ARE FOR
Paid Family Leave provides wage-replacement benefits to workers who take time off work for one of three statutory reasons: to care for a seriously ill child, spouse, parent, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, or domestic partner; to bond with a minor child within one year of the child's birth or placement in connection with foster care or adoption; or to participate in a qualifying exigency related to the covered active duty, or call to covered active duty, of the worker's spouse, domestic partner, child, or parent in the Armed Forces of the United States.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Family temporary disability insurance shall provide up to eight weeks of wage replacement benefits to workers who take time off work to care for a seriously ill child, spouse, parent, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, or domestic partner, to bond with a minor child within one year of the birth or placement of the child in connection with foster care or adoption, or to participate in a qualifying exigency related to the covered active duty or call to covered active duty of the individual’s spouse, domestic partner, child, or parent in the Armed Forces of the United States."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3301(a)(1) (leginfo text, version operative Jan. 1, 2026), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, program purpose and qualifying reasons (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3301.)
  Known gap: This is the currently operative text of Section 3301, in effect from January 1, 2026 under Stats. 2025, Ch. 772, Sec. 1 (SB 590) until a conditional repeal on or before July 1, 2028. A later version of this same section, added by Sec. 2 of that same 2025 statute, becomes operative July 1, 2028 and adds a fourth family-care-recipient category, a self-identified 'designated person,' to the list quoted here — this document reflects only the text currently in force, not that future version.

BENEFIT DURATION
Family Temporary Disability Insurance (Paid Family Leave) benefits are capped at eight weeks: no more than eight weeks of benefits may be paid within any 12-month period. The maximum amount payable during any disability benefit period is eight times the worker's weekly benefit amount, though in no case can total benefits exceed the total wages the worker was paid during the disability base period.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "No more than eight weeks of family temporary disability insurance benefits shall be paid within any 12-month period."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3301(d) (leginfo text, version operative Jan. 1, 2026), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, 12-month duration cap (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3301.)
  "The maximum amount payable to an individual during any disability benefit period for family temporary disability insurance shall be eight times the individual’s “weekly benefit amount,” but in no case shall the total amount of benefits payable be more than the total wages paid to the individual during the individual’s disability base period."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3301(c) (leginfo text, version operative Jan. 1, 2026), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, maximum benefit amount (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3301.)
  Known gap: Both citations are subsections of the same statutory section, Section 3301, and are not independent of one another. This reflects the currently operative version of Section 3301 (effective January 1, 2026 under Stats. 2025, Ch. 772, Sec. 1); a later version of this same section, not yet operative, is scheduled to take effect July 1, 2028 and retains the identical eight-week duration language as fetched. This document doesn't track how the eight-week figure has changed by amendment in years prior to this currently operative text.

WAGE-REPLACEMENT FORMULA
For periods of disability commencing on or after January 1, 2025, a worker's weekly benefit amount is calculated from the wages paid during the highest-earning quarter of the worker's disability base period. If those quarterly wages are less than $722.50, the weekly benefit amount is a flat $50. If those quarterly wages are $722.50 or more but no more than 70 percent of the state average quarterly wage, the weekly benefit amount equals 90 percent of those quarterly wages divided by 13, capped at the maximum workers' compensation temporary disability indemnity weekly benefit amount set by the Department of Industrial Relations. If those quarterly wages exceed 70 percent of the state average quarterly wage, the weekly benefit amount equals the greater of 70 percent of those quarterly wages divided by 13 (capped the same way) or 63 percent of the state average weekly wage.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "When the amount of wages paid to the individual for employment by employers during the quarter of the individual’s disability base period in which these wages were highest is less than seven hundred twenty-two dollars and fifty cents ($722.50), then fifty dollars ($50)."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3301(b)(2)(A) (leginfo text, version operative Jan. 1, 2026), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, weekly benefit amount, lowest tier (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3301.)
  "When the amount of wages paid to the individual for employment by employers during the quarter of the individual’s disability base period in which these wages were highest is seven hundred twenty-two dollars and fifty cents ($722.50) or more, but 70 percent or less than the state average quarterly wage, then the weekly benefit amount shall be equal to 90 percent of the wages paid to an individual for employment by employers during the quarter of the individual’s disability base period in which these wages were highest, divided by 13, but not exceeding the maximum workers’ compensation temporary disability indemnity weekly benefit amount established by the Department of Industrial Relations pursuant to Section 4453 of the Labor Code."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3301(b)(2)(C) (leginfo text, version operative Jan. 1, 2026), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, weekly benefit amount, middle tier (90 percent) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3301.)
  "When the amount of wages paid to the individual for employment by employers during the quarter of the individual’s disability base period in which these wages were highest is more than 70 percent of the state average quarterly wage, the weekly benefit amount shall be equal to the greater of 70 percent of the wages paid to an individual for employment by employers during the quarter of the individual’s disability base period in which these wages were highest, divided by 13, but not exceeding the maximum workers’ compensation temporary disability indemnity weekly benefit amount established by the Department of Industrial Relations pursuant to Section 4453 of the Labor Code, or 63 percent of the state average weekly wage."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3301(b)(2)(B) (leginfo text, version operative Jan. 1, 2026), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, weekly benefit amount, top tier (70/63 percent) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3301.)
  Known gap: All three citations are subsections of the same statutory section, Section 3301(b)(2), and are not independent of one another. This tiered formula took effect for periods of disability commencing on or after January 1, 2025, replacing a different, lower formula that applied to earlier periods (referenced in this same subdivision as 'the amount provided in Section 2655'), which this document doesn't independently verify or state. This document also doesn't state the current dollar value of the 'state average quarterly wage,' the 'state average weekly wage,' or the Department of Industrial Relations' maximum temporary disability indemnity rate under Labor Code Section 4453 — those figures are set and periodically adjusted outside Section 3301 itself and weren't independently fetched and verified here.

HOW PAID FAMILY LEAVE RELATES TO JOB-PROTECTED LEAVE
Paid Family Leave is a wage-replacement benefit, not a job-protection law. The Legislature's own findings draw this distinction: the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and CFRA entitle eligible employees working for covered employers to take unpaid, job-protected leave for up to 12 workweeks in a 12-month period, while state disability insurance benefits — of which Paid Family Leave is a part — provide wage replacement for time off but historically did not cover leave to care for a sick or injured family member or leave to bond with a new child. Nothing in the Paid Family Leave chapter is to be construed to abridge the rights and responsibilities conveyed under CFRA or under California's pregnancy disability leave law: Paid Family Leave and job-protected leave run on separate statutory tracks, and a worker may draw PFL wage-replacement benefits whether or not the underlying time away from work is separately job-protected.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and California’s Family Rights Act (CFRA) entitle eligible employees working for covered employers to take unpaid, job-protected leave for up to 12 workweeks in a 12-month period."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3300(d) (leginfo text), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, legislative findings on job-protected leave (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3300.)
  "State disability insurance benefits currently provide wage replacement for workers who need time off due to their own nonwork-related injuries, illnesses, or conditions, including pregnancy, that prevent them from working, but do not cover leave to care for a sick or injured child, spouse, parent, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, or domestic partner, or leave to bond with a new child."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3300(e) (leginfo text), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, legislative findings on wage replacement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3300.)
  "Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to abridge the rights and responsibilities conveyed under the California Family Rights Act or pregnancy disability leave."
  — Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code § 3301(a)(2) (leginfo text, version operative Jan. 1, 2026), California Unemployment Insurance Code, Paid Family Leave chapter, relationship to CFRA and pregnancy disability leave (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=3301.)
  Known gap: The citations to Section 3300(d) and 3300(e) are subsections of the same statutory section and are not independent of one another; the citation to Section 3301(a)(2) is to a separate, independently numbered section. Section 3300(e)'s description of what state disability insurance benefits 'do not cover' is a legislative finding explaining why the Paid Family Leave program was created, not a statement of Paid Family Leave's own current operative rules — the qualifying reasons Paid Family Leave itself covers are stated separately in Section 3301(a)(1). This document doesn't independently verify whether any CFRA- or FMLA-specific job-protection right attaches to a particular period of time an employee takes while drawing Paid Family Leave benefits; that depends on whether the underlying absence is separately CFRA- or FMLA-qualifying, which is a question for those statutes (addressed in this corpus's separate CFRA document), not for the Paid Family Leave statute itself.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Please sign below to acknowledge receipt of this information sheet regarding California's Paid Family Leave program.

Employee: Jordan Lee
Date: _______________
